question: Does adaptive job choice improve worst W inside the global-failure-threshold three-mode family, even with B knowledge?
input_scope: All5519 previously observed charged_universal_order_01 cases; every B0..7 and r0..3, no exclusions
model: While remaining slack t>0, choose any ready job and fresh prepare then cheap validate. A cheap failure decrements t and consumes one b. On t=0, use fresh preparation plus cached completion for all remaining jobs. No stored preparation, inspection or other action is modeled.
reference: Bellman over (unfinished set S,b,t); failed job may be switched. Optimizing selector is allowed to know b, making it a lower comparator for a B-blind selector within this family.
candidate: minimum-work ready job independently of b,t, repeat until it completes, then choose least-ready again
equation: X(empty,b,t)=0; X(S,0,t)=0; X(S,b,0)=Top_b(S); X(S,b,t)=min_i_ready max(X(S-i,b,t), w_i+X(S,b-1,t-1)) for b,t>0
falsifier: Any lower Bellman excess than the candidate fixed-greedy excess or any inconsistent base/transition becomes FAILURE for the proposed equality; preserve full input and both values.
